reason: Thread and planks may make a binding tool for gathering the studies.
expectation: I expect some kind of binding equipment, though its exact form is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Paper belongs in the encyclopedia, but preparing a binding tool first seems useful.

effect: The combination made a loom rather than the binding tool I expected, so I'll prepare materials at the binding table.
reaction: I was surprised by the loom; its connection to gathering the studies is not yet clear.
reason: Paper seems relevant to assembling the encyclopedia, so I'll place it at the binding table.
expectation: I expect the paper to be ready for a binding-table combination, though I don't know what it will combine with.

alternatives.reason: Planks might also be needed for binding, but paper seems more directly related to the pages.

effect: The paper is in place, and combining it with planks at the binding table is now available.
reaction: The next assembly step is clear, though its result is uncertain.
reason: The offered combination may create a structure for gathering the studies.
expectation: I expect a binding or collection component made from the paper and planks.

effect: The lined binding boards have slots for the artwork and six studies, so I can start gathering them.
reaction: The named slots make the assembly clear.
reason: Printed pages appear to fit the art slot, so I'll add them first.
expectation: I expect the printed pages to fill the art slot in the binding boards.

effect: The printed pages are fitted into the boards, leaving the other studies to gather.
reason: I'll add the pressed plant specimen to its named slot.
expectation: I expect the specimen to be fitted into the binding boards.

effect: The specimen is fitted, leaving five studies to add.
reason: The botanical drawing belongs in the next named slot.
expectation: I expect the drawing to be fitted into the binding boards.

effect: The botanical drawing is fitted, leaving four studies to add.
reason: I'll add the pond life study to its slot.
expectation: I expect the pond life study to be fitted into the binding boards.

effect: The pond life study is fitted, leaving the rain, wind and star records to add.
reaction: The repeated fittings are becoming routine.
reason: I'll add the rain record to its named slot.
expectation: I expect the rain record to be fitted into the binding boards.

effect: The rain record is fitted, leaving the wind record and star chart to add.
reason: I'll add the wind record to its named slot.
expectation: I expect the wind record to be fitted into the binding boards.

effect: The wind record is fitted, leaving the star chart to add.
reason: The star chart is the remaining named slot and the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the star chart to be fitted into the binding boards, completing the gathering goal.

effect: The star chart completed the collection, revealing the goal to bind the encyclopedia.
reaction: Gathering the studies is satisfying to finish, though the repeated fittings felt routine.
reason: Thread is the only offered combination and seems suited to binding the gathered pages.
expectation: I expect the thread to bind the boards and their contents into an encyclopedia.

effect: The thread bound the gathered material into an encyclopedia and completed the chapter.
reaction: Finishing the book was satisfying, though assembling its contents had become routine.

mostWorthwhile.text: Creating the binding boards was worthwhile because their named slots made the goal of gathering the studies concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: The successive fittings became repetitive, even though they showed the collection coming together.

surprise.text: Thread and planks made a loom when I expected a binding tool; its purpose in this chapter remained unclear.

arbitrary.text: The loom felt disconnected from the encyclopedia goal, and I did not learn a use for it.

continue.text: I would be unlikely to continue personally: the final book was satisfying, but the repeated fittings left little meaningful choice.
